TERMS OF SERVICE · VERSION 2026-11-18

The rules behind the wheel.

These Terms govern your use of THE WHEEL, a record-keeping and settlement service for private savings circles. Read them before you create an account, join a circle, or send money. By creating an account you confirm that you accept these Terms and the Privacy Notice.

1. Agreement

These Terms form a binding agreement between you and the operator of THE WHEEL (“THE WHEEL”, “we”, “us”). If you do not agree, do not create an account or join a circle. Your circle organizer may add circle-specific commitments, but nothing in a circle can remove rights you have under Kenyan law.

2. Who may use THE WHEEL

  • You must be at least 18 years old and able to enter a binding agreement.
  • You must use your real legal name and your own Kenyan phone number and national ID number.
  • One person holds one account. One national ID may not be attached to two accounts, and you may hold only one seat in the same circle.
  • You are responsible for keeping your passkey device and your recovery codes safe. Anyone with your passkey or a recovery code can act as you.

3. What THE WHEEL is — and is not

THE WHEEL records a private circle’s contributions, applies the published rules, and instructs settlement through a licensed payment provider. It is not a bank, SACCO, lender, deposit-taking institution, or investment scheme. It does not pay interest, does not lend money, and does not guarantee that any member will contribute. Money you send belongs to the circle’s settlement flow, not to a deposit account.

4. How a circle works

  • A circle has 5–12 members and a fixed contribution of KES 200–5,000 per member per turn.
  • Turns run weekly, fortnightly or monthly, as the organizer sets when the circle is created.
  • Each seat carries a posted price. The seat that takes the pot earliest accepts the largest early-bird price; the final seat accepts none. The difference between the pot and the winner’s payout is shared among the seats that waited as patience shares.
  • The pot must be fully funded before a payout is made. A turn has a 72-hour contribution window. When the last contribution lands, the turn settles and the winner is paid in the same flow.
  • A winner’s first payout is held for 48 hours before it can leave the account.
  • A bond of 10–25% of the pot is held from a winner’s payout based on trust, and is released in instalments as later turns are funded. The final turn carries no early-bird price and no bond hold.

5. Fees

Each settled pot carries a 1% platform fee and a 1% settlement-fund fee. The organizer may set an organizer fee of up to 1.5%; if the organizer wins a turn, that fee is waived back into the pot. Fees are shown in the turn’s receipt before it is final.

6. Late payments, guarantees and default

A contribution is late after a 24-hour grace period. The late fee is 2% of the contribution per day late, capped at 10%. Late fees stay inside the circle’s accounting. Members may guarantee one another, but a guarantee is a private commitment between members; THE WHEEL records it and does not lend money to cover a default.

7. Payments and payouts

  • Contributions and seat payments are collected through Paysasa and M-PESA. You authorise the provider to collect the amount shown on the checkout. We never ask for your M-PESA PIN.
  • Your stash is the balance held in your wallet for circle payments. A stash top-up is credited only after the provider confirms the payment.
  • M-PESA cash-outs are not yet open. The exact provider payout fee must be confirmed before money leaves a wallet, and this page will state the fee before withdrawals open. Until then, balances remain recorded in your wallet and can be used for contributions.
  • Provider outages, reversals and wrong-number payments are handled with the provider. We record the outcome in your ledger.

8. Leaving, refunds and seat swaps

  • Before a circle starts, you can leave and your open seat is returned to your stash.
  • An unpaid open seat that does not complete within 14 days is refunded automatically.
  • Once a circle has started, seats are final. Seats may only move through a swap that both members accept.
  • If a payment lands after the seats close, or for the wrong amount, it is returned to the payer’s stash.

9. Your data

We collect the details needed to run a circle and meet payment and identity rules. The Privacy Notice explains what is collected, why, who sees it, and the choices you have.

10. Suspension, closure and disputes

We may pause an account, seat or payout where identity details do not match, where a payment is reversed or disputed, where fraud or abuse is suspected, or where the law requires it. We keep the ledger needed to resolve the circle. Raise a disagreement inside the circle first so the organizer can record it; if it cannot be resolved there, contact the operator through your organizer. Kenyan law governs these Terms, and nothing here limits a consumer right that cannot be waived.

11. Changes

We may update these Terms as the service or the law changes. The version and date sit at the top of this page. A material change requires existing accounts to accept the new version before their next circle action. Earlier versions remain part of the account record.

12. Liability

THE WHEEL is provided with reasonable skill and care. To the extent permitted by law, we are not liable for a member’s failure to contribute, for a provider’s delay or outage, or for losses caused by a compromised passkey or recovery code. Nothing in these Terms excludes liability for fraud, wilful misconduct, or any liability that Kenyan law does not allow to be excluded.
